Zhovkva Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · L'vivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Zhovkva's Jewish community, present from the city's founding in the early 17th century, opened a Jewish printing house in 1690. Nachman Krochmal — born in Brody and later resident in Ternopil, both documented elsewhere in this collection — and Maier Letteris (1807–1871), two leading figures of the Haskalah movement in Galicia, both resided in Zhovkva. Belz Hasidism, documented elsewhere in this collection, became dominant in the second half of the 19th century. During the Soviet occupation of 1939–41, the Jewish community helped fellow Jewish refugees escape German-occupied Poland. On March 25, 1943, during the liquidation of the ghetto established in November 1942, 3,500 Jews were shot in a single day; only about 70 Jews survived to the city's liberation in July 1944.
